key_insight: Reducing the number of linear regions in ReLU neural networks, not just their size, can substantially improve optimization performance while preserving predictive accuracy.
engineering_relevance: For surrogate-based engineering optimization, especially in chemical-process superstructure problems, region-aware compression can cut solve time and help produce near-reference solutions with less computational burden.
method: Stabilize unstable ReLU neurons to simplify activation geometry.
Merge redundant neurons to reduce the number of linear regions.
Use error compensation to maintain prediction accuracy after compression.
evidence_signal: The method was evaluated on a 2D peaks function, three chemical-process surrogate models, and a hybrid superstructure optimization problem, where it reduced computational time by about 40% to 50% and kept solutions within 1% of the reference.
watch_item: Region reduction may require careful implementation to avoid degrading surrogate fidelity or missing geometry-specific effects that standard pruning does not capture.
paper_title: Optimization with Region-Reduced ReLU Neural Networks
